cards.text: Jesus is on the cross at Golgotha (Matthew 27:33). The chief priests mock Him, people passing by heap abuse on Him, and even the two robbers beside Him berate Him (Matthew 27:39-44). Then, starting at the sixth hour, something comes over all the land.

cards.question: Starting at the sixth hour, while Jesus hangs on the cross, ___ comes over all the land.

cards.text: That darkness lasts until the ninth hour. Then, about the ninth hour, Jesus cries out in a loud voice, "Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?"

cards.question: On the cross, Jesus cries out, "Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?" Who is He calling out to?

cards.text: Matthew tells us what it means: "My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?" But some of the people standing there hear it, and they think He's calling for someone else.

cards.question: When some of the people standing by the cross hear Jesus cry "Eli, Eli," who do they think He is calling?

cards.text: Elijah, the prophet from long ago (1 Kings 18:36). Then one of them quickly runs and brings a sponge.

cards.question: One of the people standing by the cross fills the sponge with ___, puts it on a reed and holds it up for Jesus to drink.

cards.text: But the others standing there? They have a whole different idea.

cards.question: The others at the cross tell the man with the sponge to hurry up and give Jesus the drink.

cards.text: They say, "Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to save Him." Then Jesus cries out again in a loud voice.

cards.question: On the cross, Jesus cries out again in a loud voice. What happens next?

answers.text: He comes down from the cross

cards.text: Jesus has yielded up His spirit, and at that very moment, something happens. Not at the cross, friend, at the temple.

cards.question: At the moment Jesus yields up His spirit, what happens to the veil of the temple?
When Jesus yields up His spirit, the veil of the temple tears from the bottom up.

cards.text: Then the earth quakes, and the rocks split.

cards.question: When Jesus dies, the tombs break open. What happens to the bodies of many saints who had fallen asleep?

cards.text: These saints come out of the tombs, enter the holy city and appear to many people. But Matthew ties the timing to something in Jesus' story that hasn't happened yet.

cards.question: The saints who were raised come out of the tombs and go into the holy city before Jesus' resurrection.

cards.text: Back at the cross, a centurion, a Roman officer, has been guarding Jesus with his men. They see the earthquake and all that has happened.

cards.question: When they see the earthquake and all that has happened, the centurion and those guarding Jesus with him are ___.
Terrified, the centurion and those with him say something about Jesus. What do they say?

answers.text: Truly this was the Son of God
Truly this was a great prophet
Truly this was the King of Israel

cards.text: The people passing by heaped abuse on Him with that same title (Matthew 27:39-40). Now the very men guarding Him are the ones saying it.
And many women are there too, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus all the way from Galilee.

cards.question: Many women watch the cross from a distance. Why had they followed Jesus from Galilee?
Mary Magdalene is among the women watching from a distance.

cards.text: Mary Magdalene, the woman seven demons had gone out of (Luke 8:2), is there with Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee's sons, the apostles James and John (Matthew 10:2). We'll stop here for now, friend, but this story is NOT over.

findings.problem: The setup on card 9 says the others 'have a whole different idea' from the man with the sponge. That rules out the statement that they tell him to hurry up and give Jesus the drink, so the true or false answer is given away before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Matthew 27:47 says the bystanders 'said, "He is calling Elijah."' It never says what they thought. Card 5 ('they think He's calling for someone else') and the card 6 question ('who do they think He is calling?') state their belief as fact. The text leaves that open. Word both cards as what they say, for example 'who do they say He is calling?'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: 'Then the earth quakes' adds a sequence. Matthew 27:51 puts the torn veil, the earthquake and the split rocks together under 'At that moment.' It does not say the quake came afterward.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: Cards 4 ('Then the earth quakes, and the rocks split.') and 5 ('And the tombs break open.') are bare one-line summaries with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Card 5 adds nothing that the card 6 question doesn't repeat. Merge them into one story card with a storyteller's touch.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Card 7 says Matthew 'ties the timing to something in Jesus' story that hasn't happened yet.' This all but tells the baker that the saints entered the city after the resurrection. It rules out 'True' before the baker answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Nothing before this card gives a reason to choose 'the Son of God' over 'a great prophet' or 'the King of Israel,' so the pick comes down to luck. The setup that would help, the mockers using that title (Matthew 27:40, 43), comes only afterward on card 12. Move that setup before the question, or give card 9 more context.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Mary Magdalene first shows up in this true or false question, with no word on who she is. She is only introduced afterward on card 16. With no setup naming any of the women, the pick is also pure luck.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
